verdict: Needs small polish, not a material redesign. The safest product meaning of "nothing is blocked; any valid deck should work" is that HSConfig should autonomously produce a structurally valid, load-safe initial HearthRanger CustomConfig package for any valid deck input that can be decoded and represented inside the normal HSConfig runtime surface contract. It must not mean that every deck is SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, fully optimized, combo-complete, future-mechanic-complete, guide-perfect, or tuned from runtime evidence. Technical invalidity still blocks. Source-depth debt, warning-only mechanics, unknown future mechanics, missing guide strength, combo uncertainty, and runtime-evidence-only tuning stay visible as warnings, reports, or non-strong semantic statuses while load_safe_apply remains allowed for VALID_PACKAGE outputs.

provided_deck_matrix_assessment: The provided deck set is sufficient for the current no-block product claim because it exercises package generation across twelve valid Wild inputs while separating the representative source-depth matrix from supplemental acceptance proof.

The eleven representative rows cover aggro burn, recruit board flood, pirate tempo, big cheat, discard, token board, hero-power generation, mech scaling, weapon sequence, combo control, and pirate hero attack. That is broad enough for a lean pre-run CustomConfig proof without attempting to cover every possible Wild family.

Kingslayer and Boarlock are useful precisely because they are not hidden as perfect rows. Kingslayer preserves the Quick Pick mulligan and unsupported-condition gap. Boarlock preserves the Fracking mulligan gap plus runtime-surface, generic-low-confidence, uncovered-card, and unsupported-condition debt. They prove visible failure modes, not universal strongness.

CuteWarrior adds a supplemental Warrior low-curve acceptance proof without bloating the representative matrix. It should remain supplemental unless a future matrix review proves it covers a missing pre-run family none of the eleven rows expose.

The matrix proves the runtime package promise for the listed valid decks: prepare succeeds, package validation passes, load_safe_apply is allowed, required runtime files exist, per-card rich output exists when identity is known, and normal-path Presume.json and Concede.json are absent.

The matrix does not and should not claim full deck-universe exhaustiveness. Its role is to prove the product boundary and catch regressions in the no-block contract, while mechanic drift and warning surfaces handle unknown future cards without expanding the fixture set for every keyword.
no_block_assessment: Technical invalidity remains a hard block. Malformed or unsupported deckcodes, undecodable or unresolved required identity, invalid JSON, unsupported runtime filenames or blocks, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, undeclared runtime files, nested runtime files, normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json, missing operator_summary.json, forged gates, stale summaries, or package validation failures must stop runtime apply.

Warning-only mechanics are not blocks. A valid package can name Dredge, Tradeable, board position, generic spell targeting, location activation, secret timing, generated-entity random pools, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, Shatter, or unknown future mechanics as report-only visibility while still remaining load-safe.

Source-depth gaps are not runtime blocks. Missing guide claims, missing mulligan specificity, source evidence warnings, static-semantics fallback, generic-low-confidence cards, uncovered cards, and guide-depth weakness prevent SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG or promotion, but they do not block load_safe_apply when the package is technically valid.

Unsupported future mechanics are warning-only until mapped. HSConfig should detect unknown mechanics and unknown card types, expose first_unknown_mechanic or first_unknown_card_type through mechanic_drift_summary, and recommend inspection without inventing runtime rows or refusing the package solely because the future mechanic is unmapped.

Missing guide strength should reduce semantic strength, not autonomy. VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE, READY_TO_APPLY_WITH_WARNINGS, config_usefulness usable_with_targeted_gaps, and load_safe_but_thin are acceptable outcomes for any valid deck when the runtime JSON remains valid.

Combo uncertainty should be exact-only. Combo.json is appropriate when ordered sequence, operators, values, and conditions are source-backed or statically exact. Vague combo advice, missing timing, unsupported conditions, or ambiguous generated entities should be suppressed into reports and may block SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, but they should not block the base load-safe package.

Runtime-evidence-only tuning is outside HSConfig. GlobalValues keys or strategic changes that require games, logs, winrate, replay review, or post-run candidate promotion should stay blocked_until_runtime_evidence in reports and should not cause HSConfig to call HSTuner, parse replays, or refuse a valid pre-run package.

The product phrase should be documented as: no valid deck is blocked from receiving a safe initial package merely because source confidence, mechanic lowering, combo precision, or config richness is incomplete. It should never be shortened to: every deck is strong, optimized, fully lowered, or proven in live HearthRanger runtime.
skill_slimness_assessment: The current skill boundary is slim and correct: HSConfig is pre-run only, starts from deck identity and guide/source evidence, emits normal CustomConfig runtime files and reports, validates the package, and uses operator_summary.json as the single gate.
The skill avoids HSranger or HSTuner scope creep. It does not parse Power.log, .hdtreplay, .hsreplay, runtime logs, gameplay outcomes, winrate, or post-game candidate evidence.

The normal runtime surface set remains understandable: required GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json, rich per-card CardID JSON files when deck identity is known, optional exact Combo.json, and no normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json.

The warning model keeps autonomy high without adding risky runtime rows. HSConfig reports warning-only mechanics, mechanic drift, unsupported claims, source gaps, suppressed combos, and runtime-evidence-only GlobalValues changes instead of expanding the writer.

The existing docs and tests already prevent over-conservatism by making load_safe_apply depend on technical validity rather than SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG. The smallest improvement should reuse this structure instead of adding more representative decks or broadening the runtime surface registry.

The installed skill and repo operator docs are aligned on the main contract. The remaining slimness risk is operator wording: phrases like source-informed blocked, semantic blockers, and no-block can look contradictory unless failure modes are grouped clearly.
hearthstone_semantic_coverage: Static coverage is appropriate for pre-run package generation: HSConfig uses card identity, card text, mechanics, referenced tags, archetype roles, hero power links, generated entities, and source-backed claims to decide what can be lowered into normal VisionAI surfaces.

Mechanic coverage is layered instead of binary. Direct mechanics can emit known runtime rows; identity-gated-direct mechanics such as discover or choose_one need exact option identity; partial mechanics can emit only safe posture or known pieces; warning-only mechanics stay report-only.

Current tests cover older Wild families such as questline, highlander, outcast, infuse, corrupt, finale, manathirst, forge, excavate, plague, titan, colossal, dormant, invoke, jade, C'Thun package, spell school, dredge, tradeable, magnetic, and generated entities.

Current tests also cover modern text-only or keyword families including kindred, tourist, starship, spellburst, miniaturize, quickdraw, honorable_kill, elusive, poisonous, imbue, rewind, herald, and shatter. Rewind, herald, shatter, starship, kindred, and tourist currently remain warning-only where no safe normal-path runtime surface exists.

Exact CardID handling is a technical requirement, not a richness preference. Public HearthSim docs warn that CardIDs are inconsistent and case-sensitive, so any valid package must preserve exact card identity before writing per-card runtime files.

Generated entities and random pools are handled conservatively: known generated identities can be represented partially or through identity-gated rows, while unresolved random pools remain warning-only so the skill does not invent unavailable choices.

Hero-power and deckwide mechanics are covered through card behavior and GlobalValues posture where safe, but runtime-evidence-only tuning remains outside HSConfig and stays report-only until games or runtime evidence exist.

[uncertain] No static matrix can prove every future Hearthstone mechanic, every future Wild deck family, or every future HearthRanger parser behavior. The safe product posture is therefore drift visibility plus load-safe fallback, not exhaustive first-class lowering.
gaps_or_risks: The public HearthRanger VisionAI documentation is old and partly forum-based. It is still useful for surface boundaries, but exact live runtime parser behavior may drift without notice.

[uncertain] A future Hearthstone mechanic or card type could require a new runtime surface to be truly strong. The current no-block contract handles this by reporting unknown mechanics and unknown card types as non-blocking drift, but it cannot pre-prove first-class support before the mechanic exists in data.

The universal proof matrix covers twelve named valid Wild inputs, not every valid deck code in the universe. That is acceptable for regression proof, but the product wording must avoid universal gameplay-quality claims.

[uncertain] This audit did not run HearthRanger itself or inspect live bot logs. The evidence proves HSConfig package validation and apply-gate behavior, not live gameplay improvement or runtime execution quality.

The words blocker, source-informed blocked, semantic_blockers, and no-block can confuse operators because some blockers prevent SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG while not blocking load_safe_apply. That is a terminology and reporting risk, not a technical gate defect.

Combo coverage remains intentionally narrow. Boarlock is the only representative Combo.json control row, so combo breadth should not be overstated; vague combo advice must remain suppressed until exact ordered sequences are available.

If future work broadens Presume.json, Concede.json, unsupported condition syntax, or generated-choice lowering without keeping the apply gate strict, the no-block promise could become unsafe rather than autonomous.
If future work responds to warning-only mechanics by blocking load_safe_apply, the skill would become over-conservative and would violate the intended any-valid-deck package promise.
